**ʿArḍa l-ḥayāti l-dunyā** (﴿the commodity of worldly life﴾): i.e., wealth.

**Wa-man yukrihhunna** (﴿And whoever compels them﴾): i.e., to prostitution (*al-zinā*, fornication).

**Mubayyinātin** (﴿clear﴾): explaining the rulings, clarifying what is required of you to do and to avoid.

**Wa-mathalan min alladhīna khalaw min qablikum** (﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾): i.e., before you; that is, narratives from the accounts of earlier peoples, such as the story of Joseph and the story of Mary, both of which resemble the incident of the slander (*ḥādithat al-ifk*).

**Wa-mawʿiẓatan** (﴿and an admonition﴾): *al-mawʿiẓa* is that by which the servant is admonished so that he follows the path of salvation.

---

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

The context continues to deal with the means that protect against the commission of indecency. In the first verse of this context [32], Allah, exalted is He, commands the community of Muslims to marry off the unmarried among their men and women, by assisting in that and helping to bring it about, so that no single man or woman remains unmarried in the city or village except rarely. There is no difference in this between the virgin and the previously married. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And marry off﴾ — the command here is one of guidance — ﴿the unmarried﴾, the plural of *ayyim*, which refers to the man or woman who has no spouse, whether virgin or previously married, ﴿among you﴾, i.e., among the communities of Muslims, not among others such as the *ahl al-dhimma* (protected non-Muslim subjects) of the disbelievers. His saying: ﴿and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾, i.e., marry off those among your slaves who are able to bear the expenses and obligations of marriage. His saying: ﴿If they are poor﴾, not wealthy, that should not prevent you from marrying them, for Allah has guaranteed their enrichment after marriage by His saying: ﴿Allah will enrich them from His bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, i.e., abundant in bounty, knowing the needs of the needy.

In this verse, Allah, exalted is He, commanded whoever cannot find a marriage, either because of the temporary absence of a spouse or because of the lack of the means of marriage such as the dowry and the wedding feast, to keep himself chaste, i.e., to restrain himself through patience, fasting and prayer, so that he does not look toward the forbidden and thus perish. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And let those who cannot find marriage keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾, i.e., He is abundant in bounty, absolutely rich, knowing the condition of His servants and the needs of the needy among them.

His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And those who seek a deed of manumission﴾. This is a third matter included in this verse: if a Muslim has a slave who asks him for a *mukātaba*, and the slave is suitable for freedom, being able to pay the amount of the *mukātaba* and able to be independent by himself, then his master must make a *mukātaba* contract with him and help him in that by remitting one of the installments of the contract. This is the meaning of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And those who seek a deed of manumission from among those whom your right hands possess — write it for them if you know any good in them, and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾.

His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, i.e., to fornication. This is a fourth matter included in this verse: two slave girls belonging to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, the hypocrite, named Muʿādha and Musaykah, had embraced Islam, and he ordered them to fornicate so that they would earn for him through their private parts, as was the custom of the people of pre-Islamic ignorance. They complained of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity, in order to seek the commodity of worldly life﴾, i.e., for the sake of a small amount of wealth that is presented to you and quickly passes away from you. His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them — indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e., toward them, Merciful to them, because the one who is compelled bears no sin for what he says or what he does. The hypocrite thus refrained from that.

Regarding His, exalted is He, saying in the second verse [34]: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that are clear﴾, i.e., We have sent down to you, O Muslims, verses, meaning Qur'anic verses, that are clear, i.e., explaining the laws, rulings and ethics. So act upon them, that you may be perfected in your lives and be happy in your worldly life and your Hereafter. His saying: ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾, i.e., narratives from the accounts of earlier peoples, such as the story of Joseph and the story of Mary, peace be upon them, both of which resemble the incident of the slander. His saying: ﴿and an admonition for the righteous﴾, which is what the verses contain of threat and promise, encouragement and warning. That they are for the righteous is in accordance with reality, for the righteous are those who benefit from admonitions, unlike the disbelievers and the wicked.

---

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The obligation on Muslims, rulers and ruled alike, to help in marrying off the unmarried among the Muslims, whether free or slaves.
2. The obligation of chastity upon whoever cannot find marriage, and of patience until Allah eases his affair.
3. Allah's promise to the poor who marry that He will make them wealthy.
4. The requirement to grant manumission to a slave when the conditions of *mukātaba* are met.
5. The prohibition of fornication, whether under compulsion or by choice, and the prevention of it through the enforcement of the prescribed punishments (*ḥudūd*).
6. The form of the *mukātaba* contract: the master says to the slave, "I have made a *mukātaba* with you for three thousand dinars, payable in six installments, one installment to be paid each month. If you pay it on its due dates, you are free." And it is witnessed and dated accordingly.
7. Explanation of the virtue of Surah al-Nur because of the very important rulings it contains.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verse 35–38:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Allahu nuru as-samawati wal-ard﴾: that is, the One who illuminates them. Were it not for Him, there would be no light in the heavens or on the earth. God, exalted is He, is Light, and His veil is light.

﴿Mathalu nurihi﴾: that is, in the heart of His believing servant.

﴿Ka-mishkat﴾: that is, a niche (kawwa) in a wall.

﴿Kawkabun durri﴾: that is, shining with the brilliance of a radiant pearl.

﴿Nurun ʿala nur﴾: that is, the light of the fire upon the light of the oil.

﴿Yahdi Allahu li-nurihi﴾: that is, guides to belief in Him and to acting in obedience to Him whomever He wills, because He knows their desire and the sincerity of their intention.

﴿Wa yadribu Allahu al-amthal﴾: that is, God sets forth parables for people so that they may understand from Him and comprehend what He calls them to.

﴿Fi buyutin adhina Allahu an turfa'﴾: these are the mosques, and their elevation means exalting their status through construction, purity and maintenance.

﴿Yawman tatagallabu fihi al-qulubu wal-absar﴾: the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Yarzuqu man yasha'u bi-ghayri hisab﴾: that is, without counting, measuring or weighing; this is the nature of a gift when it is abundant.

Meaning of the verses:

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Allahu nuru as-samawati wal-ard﴾. He informs that were it not for Him there would be no light in the universe nor any guidance in the heavens or on the earth. He is the One who illuminates them. His Book is light and His Messenger is light, by which one is guided through the darknesses of life just as one is guided by physical light. God Himself is light and His veil is light. Every light, whether physical or spiritual, is created and bestowed by God and leads to Him.

And His saying: ﴿Mathalu nurihi ka-mishkatin﴾: that is, like a niche in a wall, ﴿fihi misbah al-misbahu fi zujajah﴾: a lamp in a glass of crystal, ﴿al-zujajatu ka-annaha kawkabun durriyyun﴾: the glass, in its clarity and polish, shining as if it were a radiant star. The "durri" star is the bright, luminous one, as if it were a white, pure pearl. And His saying: ﴿Yuqadu min shajaratin mubarakatin﴾: that is, the oil of the lamp comes from a blessed tree, which is the olive tree. The olive tree is neither eastern nor western in its position in the orchard: it is not exposed to the sun only in the morning, nor is it western, seeing the sun only in the evening, but it stands in the middle of the orchard, touched by the sun throughout the day. Therefore its oil is of the utmost quality, nearly bursting into flame because of its purity, even if no fire touches it. And His saying: ﴿Nurun ʿala nur﴾: that is, the light of the fire upon the light of the oil.

And His saying: ﴿Yahdi Allahu li-nurihi man yasha'u﴾: God informs that He guides to His light, which is faith, Islam and excellence, whomever He wills of His servants, those whom He knows to desire guidance, seek it, perfect themselves and find happiness through it.

And His saying: ﴿Wa yadribu Allahu al-amthala lin-nasi wallahu bi-kulli shay'in ʿalim﴾: God informs that He sets forth parables for people, like this parable He set forth for faith and the heart of His believing servant, and that He is All-Knowing of His servants and the states of hearts, and of who is fit for guidance and who is not, for He has knowledge of everything.

And His saying: ﴿Fi buyutin adhina Allahu an turfa'﴾: that is, the lamp is in houses which God has permitted, that is, commanded and enjoined, to be raised, both physically and in meaning. These are the mosques, which are purified from impurities, from idle talk and worldly speech, and are preserved and guarded from everything that would diminish their lofty station, because they are the houses of God, exalted is He. And His saying: ﴿Wa yudhkara fiha ismuhu﴾: that is, through the adhan, the iqamah, prayer, glorification, supplication and recitation of the Qur'an.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Yusabbihu lahu fiha﴾: that is, glorifying God in those houses ﴿bil-ghuduwwi﴾: that is, in the morning ﴿wal-asal﴾: that is, in the evening. ﴿Rijalun﴾: men who are believing, truthful, righteous and God-fearing ﴿la tulhihim tijaratun wa la bay'un﴾: that is, neither buying nor selling ﴿ʿan dhikri Allah﴾: so their hearts remember and are not heedless, and their tongues remember and are neither idle nor frivolous ﴿wa iqami as-salati wa itai az-zakah﴾: that is, their worldly affairs do not distract them from their hereafter, so they establish prayer and give zakah.

And His saying: ﴿Yakhafuna yawman tatagallabu fihi al-qulubu wal-absar﴾: that is, out of intense fear and great terror and dread, and this is the Day of Resurrection. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Liyajziyahumu Allahu ahsana ma ʿamilu wa yazidahum min fadlihi﴾: that is, they did what they did of glorification, establishing prayer and giving zakah, turning away from everything that would occupy them from worshipping their Lord, and thereby they became fit for the great reward, so that God may recompense them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty beyond what they deserved by their deeds and their piety toward their Lord. And God gives to whomever He wills without reckoning, and that is because of His great bounty and His preceding mercy, so He gives without counting, measuring or weighing, and that is because of the greatness and abundance of the gift.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Every good, every light and every guidance comes from God, exalted is He, so it is from Him alone that it should be sought.

2- The commendability of setting forth parables to bring meanings closer to minds and understanding.

3- An indication that the religion of Islam is neither Judaism nor Christianity, neither socialism nor capitalism, but the upright monotheistic religion (al-hanifiyyah): whoever adheres to it is guided, and whoever rejects it has gone astray.

4- The obligation to honor the houses of God, the mosques, by purifying them, maintaining their structures, and keeping them free except for the remembrance of God, prayer and the seeking of knowledge within them.

5- The praise of God for those whom trade and commerce do not distract from the remembrance of God, the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah.

And His saying: ﴿Mathalu nurihi ka-mishkatin﴾: that is, like a niche in a wall, ﴿fihi misbah al-misbahu fi zujajah﴾: a lamp in a glass of crystal, ﴿al-zujajatu ka-annaha kawkabun durriyyun﴾: the glass, in its clarity and polish, shining as if it were a radiant star. The "durri" star is the bright, luminous one, as if it were a white, pure pearl. And His saying: ﴿Yuqadu min shajaratin mubarakatin﴾: that is, the oil of the lamp comes from a blessed tree, which is the olive tree. The olive tree is neither eastern nor western in its position in the orchard: it is not exposed to the sun only in the morning, nor is it western, seeing the sun only in the evening, but it stands in the middle of the orchard, touched by the sun throughout the day. Therefore its oil is of the utmost quality, nearly bursting into flame because of its purity, even if no fire touches it. And His saying: ﴿Nurun ʿala nur﴾: that is, the light of the fire upon the light of the oil.

And His saying: ﴿Yahdi Allahu li-nurihi man yasha'u﴾: God informs that He guides to His light, which is faith, Islam and excellence, whomever He wills of His servants, those whom He knows to desire guidance, seek it, perfect themselves and find happiness through it.

And His saying: ﴿Wa yadribu Allahu al-amthala lin-nasi wallahu bi-kulli shay'in ʿalim﴾: God informs that He sets forth parables for people, like this parable He set forth for faith and the heart of His believing servant, and that He is All-Knowing of His servants and the states of hearts, and of who is fit for guidance and who is not, for He has knowledge of everything.

And His saying: ﴿Fi buyutin adhina Allahu an turfa'﴾: that is, the lamp is in houses which God has permitted, that is, commanded and enjoined, to be raised, both physically and in meaning. These are the mosques, which are purified from impurities, from idle talk and worldly speech, and are preserved and guarded from everything that would diminish their lofty station, because they are the houses of God, exalted is He. And His saying: ﴿Wa yudhkara fiha ismuhu﴾: that is, through the adhan, the iqamah, prayer, glorification, supplication and recitation of the Qur'an.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Yusabbihu lahu fiha﴾: that is, glorifying God in those houses ﴿bil-ghuduwwi﴾: that is, in the morning ﴿wal-asal﴾: that is, in the evening. ﴿Rijalun﴾: men who are believing, truthful, righteous and God-fearing ﴿la tulhihim tijaratun wa la bay'un﴾: that is, neither buying nor selling ﴿ʿan dhikri Allah﴾: so their hearts remember and are not heedless, and their tongues remember and are neither idle nor frivolous ﴿wa iqami as-salati wa itai az-zakah﴾: that is, their worldly affairs do not distract them from their hereafter, so they establish prayer and give zakah.

And His saying: ﴿Yakhafuna yawman tatagallabu fihi al-qulubu wal-absar﴾: that is, out of intense fear and great terror and dread, and this is the Day of Resurrection. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Liyajziyahumu Allahu ahsana ma ʿamilu wa yazidahum min fadlihi﴾: that is, they did what they did of glorification, establishing prayer and giving zakah, turning away from everything that would occupy them from worshipping their Lord, and thereby they became fit for the great reward, so that God may recompense them with the best of what they did and increase them from His bounty beyond what they deserved by their deeds and their piety toward their Lord. And God gives to whomever He wills without reckoning, and that is because of His great bounty and His preceding mercy, so He gives without counting, measuring or weighing, and that is because of the greatness and abundance of the gift.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Every good, every light and every guidance comes from God, exalted is He, so it is from Him alone that it should be sought.

2- The commendability of setting forth parables to bring meanings closer to minds and understanding.

3- An indication that the religion of Islam is neither Judaism nor Christianity, neither socialism nor capitalism, but the upright monotheistic religion (al-hanifiyyah): whoever adheres to it is guided, and whoever rejects it has gone astray.

4- The obligation to honor the houses of God, the mosques, by purifying them, maintaining their structures, and keeping them free except for the remembrance of God, prayer and the seeking of knowledge within them.

5- The praise of God for those whom trade and commerce do not distract from the remembrance of God, the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 39–42:

Explanation of the words:

Kasarab bi-qay'a: the sarab (mirage) is a white ray seen at midday that appears to be water, and qay'a is the plural of qa', which is the flat expanse of land.

Al-zam'an: the thirsty one.

Bahr lujji: that which has lujaj (deep waters), and the lujja is the main and abundant body of water, as is the case in oceans.

Yaghshahu mawj: a wave covers it and rises above it.

Yusabbihu lahu: glorifies and sanctifies Him with words of tasbih and taqdis, such as "Subhan Allah" and the like; and prayer (salah) is also a form of tasbih.

Saffat: spreading out their wings.

Qad 'alima salatahu: that is, everyone in the heavens and the earth has known God's prayer and glorification, just as every one who glorifies and prays knows the prayer and glorification of himself.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage﴾. When the Most High explained the condition of the believers, and that He pays them their reward in the best manner of what they used to do, and increases them from His bounty, He here mentioned the condition of the disbelievers: that their deeds, in their loss and their failure to benefit from them, are like a mirage, which is a white ray seen at midday that appears to be water. ﴿In a valley (bi-qay'a)﴾, that is, in an expanse of land, which is flat ground. ﴿The thirsty one thinks it to be water﴾, that is, the thirsty one supposes it to be water, and it is not water, but a deceptive mirage. ﴿Until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾, because it is a mirage and nothing more. Alas for the disappointment, the disappointment of a thirsty man whom thirst is killing: he sees a mirage and runs after it, thinking it to be water, but when he reaches it he finds no water, and he finds Allah, blessed and exalted, who calls him to account for all his deeds, which in their totality are deeds of crime, evil and corruption, and repays him for them, so he loses with a manifest loss. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. Then it is but moments before the disbeliever is in the midst of Hellfire. This is a parable contained in the first verse [39], and another parable contained in the second verse [40], which is a parable struck for the misguidance of the disbeliever and his bewilderment in his life, and what he lives upon of the darkness of disbelief, the darkness of evil deeds, false belief, and the darkness of ignorance of his Lord and of what He wants from him and what He has prepared for him. The Most High said: ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea (bahr lujjiyy)﴾, that is, one having lujaj of water, ﴿covered by waves﴾, that is, the waves rise above it, ﴿above which are waves, above which is cloud﴾, that is, above the wave is another wave, ﴿above which is cloud﴾. Clouds are usually dark, so these are ﴿darknesses, one above another; when he extends his hand, he can hardly see it﴾ because of the intensity of the darkness. This is the condition of the disbeliever in this worldly life, and it results from his turning away from the remembrance of his Lord and his immersion in evil and corruption. And the words of the Most High: ﴿And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾. He, the Most High, informed His servants that light belongs to Him and is in His hand, so whoever does not seek it from Him is deprived of it and lives in darknesses, and we seek refuge with Allah.

And the words of the Most High: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah is glorified by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight?﴾ That is, has it not reached your knowledge, O Our Messenger, that Allah, the Most High, is glorified by whoever is in the heavens, from among the angels, and the earth, that is, and whoever is on the earth, by the tongue of speech and of state together. ﴿And the birds in flight (saffat)﴾, that is, spreading out their wings, glorify Allah, the Most High, meaning they declare Him far above imperfection with words of glorification such as "Subhan Allah."

If the polytheists, the people of darknesses, refuse to believe in Allah and to worship Him and to affirm His oneness, then Allah, the Most High, is glorified by all creation, above and below. The disbeliever, even if he does not glorify with his tongue, his state glorifies: his creation, his composition, his words and his deeds all glorify Allah his Creator, and they bear witness to the power, knowledge and wisdom of Allah, and that there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. And the words of the Most High: ﴿Each one (kullun)﴾, that is, of those in the heavens and the earth and the birds, has known Allah's prayer and glorification, just as each of them has known his own prayer to Allah and his glorification of Him. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what they do﴾, that is, Allah is knowing of the actions of His servants, and He recompenses them for them, and He is capable of that, since to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Him is the final return, that is, the return of everything is to Him, the Most High, and He is the One who judges in it with His just judgment.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The recommendation of coining parables to bring distant meanings closer to understanding.

2- Explanation of the loss of the disbelievers in their deeds and their whole life.

3- Explanation of the condition of the disbelievers in this world, that they live in darknesses of ignorance, disbelief and wrongdoing.

4- Establishing the truth that whoever Allah has not made a light in his heart will have no light in his whole life.

5- Explanation that the whole universe glorifies Allah, as in the words of the Most High: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him﴾ [al-Hashr: 24], and His words: ﴿And there is not a thing but it glorifies Him by His praise﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 43–46:

Explanation of the words:

*Yuzjee sahaban* (drives clouds): i.e., drives them gently and easily.

*Thumma yu'allifu baynahu* (then joins them together): i.e., gathers their parts and pieces together.

*Thumma yaj'aluhu rukaman* (then makes it heaped up): i.e., piled up, some of it upon the other.

*Al-wadq* (the rain): i.e., the rain.

*Yakhruju min khilalihi* (comes forth from within it): i.e., from its openings and gaps.

*Min jibalin fiha min barad* (from mountains of hail therein): i.e., from mountains of hail in the sky. Al-barad is white stones, like snow.

*Fa yusibu bihi man yasha'* (so He strikes with it whom He wills): i.e., He strikes with the hail whom He wills.

*Sana barqihi* (the flash of its lightning): i.e., its brightness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 47–52:

Explanation of the words:

"And they say": that is, the hypocrites (munafiqun).

"We believe in Allah and in the Messenger": that is, we affirm the Oneness of Allah and the prophethood of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

"Then a group of them turn away": that is, they turn away (ya'riD).

"When a group of them are turning away": that is, from coming to the Messenger (ﷺ).

"Prone (mudh'inin)": that is, hastening, submitting, obedient.

"In their hearts is a disease": that is, disbelief, hypocrisy and polytheism.

"Or do they have doubt": that is, rather, they doubt the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ).

"That Allah should wrong them, and His Messenger": that is, in judgment, so that they would be treated unjustly in it.

"The saying of the believers was only": it is their saying, "We hear and we obey," that is, hearing and obedience.

"The successful (al-muflihun)": that is, those who win salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

After presenting those manifestations of Allah's power, knowledge and wisdom which necessitate faith in Allah and His Messenger, and what is with Allah of lasting bliss and what He has of humiliating punishment, some were guided by them, whom Allah willed to guide, and others turned away from them, whose wretchedness Allah had decreed, from among the hypocrites, about whom the Most High informed with His saying: ﴿And they say, "We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey"﴾, that is, we affirm Allah as Lord and God, and Muhammad as Prophet and Messenger, and we obey both of them. ﴿Then a group of them turn away after that﴾, that is, after their declaration of faith and obedience, they say, turning away in their hearts from faith in Allah, His signs and His Messenger, ﴿and those are not believers﴾, so Allah refuted them in their claim of this faith. This is what the first verse [47] indicates. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them﴾, that is, in a matter of their worldly affairs, ﴿behold, a group of them are turning away﴾, that is, a group of them surprised you by turning away from appealing to the Messenger (ﷺ). And His saying: ﴿But if the right was theirs﴾, that is, if the right was theirs in the dispute between them and others, ﴿they would come to him﴾, that is, to the Messenger of Allah, ﴿willingly submitting﴾, that is, submitting and obedient, because they know that the Messenger judges between them with truth and they will take their right in full. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease?﴾, that is, rather, there is in their hearts the disease of disbelief and hypocrisy. ﴿Or have they doubted?﴾, that is, rather, they doubted, that is, they were in doubt about the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿Or do they fear that Allah will wrong them and His Messenger?﴾ No, no. ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾ And because they are wrongdoers, they fear the judgment of Allah and His Messenger regarding them, for He is just, and He takes from them what is not theirs and gives it to those among their adversaries who are entitled to it. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them, is only that they say, "We hear and we obey."﴾, that is, the sincere believers in their faith. The believers had no saying to say when called to the Book of Allah and His Messenger to judge between them except their saying, "We hear and we obey," so they answer the call and submit to the truth. The Most High said in praise of them: ﴿And those are the successful﴾, that is, the prosperous in their worldly life and their Hereafter, not others among the people of hypocrisy. And His saying, exalted is He, in the last noble verse [52]: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, in what they command and forbid, ﴿and fears Allah﴾, that is, fears Him openly and secretly, ﴿and is conscious of Him﴾, that is, guards against disobeying Him, so he neglects no obligation and does not commit what is forbidden, ﴿those are the attainers [of success]﴾. The restriction of success to them means that they are the ones secure from the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, enjoying the Gardens of Bliss with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.

O Allah, make us among them and gather us in their company, for You are our Lord and their Lord.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of judging by the Book and the Sunnah.

2- Whoever is called to the Book and the Sunnah and turns away is a hypocrite of known hypocrisy.

3- Adopting man-made laws to judge by, instead of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, is a sign of disbelief and hypocrisy.

4- The virtue of obeying Allah and His Messenger and fearing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that its people are the successful, saved from the Fire and admitted to the Gardens.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 53–55:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And they swore by God, their most solemn oaths﴾: i.e., they swore by God, exerting the utmost effort in their oaths.

﴿If you command them﴾: i.e., to go out to jihad.

﴿Obedience is known﴾: i.e., a known obedience to the Prophet in what he commands you and forbids you is better than your swearing by God.

﴿But if you turn away﴾: i.e., if you turn away, that is, you turn aside from obedience.

﴿Upon him is what he has been charged with﴾: i.e., the conveying of the message and its clarification by word and deed.

﴿And upon you is what you have been charged with﴾: i.e., the obligation to accept the Law and act upon it in belief, worship and judgment.

﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾: i.e., if you obey the Messenger in his command, his prohibition and his guidance, you will be guided to your own good.

﴿He will surely make them successors﴾: i.e., He will make them successors to others in the land, by replacing its former inhabitants for them, so that they will rule and govern it.

﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion﴾: i.e., by making Islam prevail over all other religions and preserving it from extinction.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of the state of the hypocrites. God informs about them with His words: ﴿And they swore by God, their most solemn oaths﴾, i.e., they swore to the Messenger ﷺ, exerting themselves to the utmost, saying: "If you command us to go out to jihad, we will surely go out with you." Here God commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Do not swear﴾, i.e., there is no need for oaths and their emphasis; rather, what is required is a known obedience from you to us, which will suffice you instead of oaths. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do﴾ is a rebuke and a discipline for them, as God informed them that He is aware of their secrets and of what they say and do in secret against the Messenger and the believers. Then God commanded His Messenger to say to them: Obey God and obey the Messenger in all that they command and forbid. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., you turn aside from obedience and reject it, then upon the Messenger is only what he has been charged with of conveying and clarifying, and upon you is what you have been charged with of the obligation to submit and obey. Whoever neglects his duty with which he has been entrusted will meet his recompense in full before his Lord.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾ — this sentence is great in importance and noble in worth for the believer, who swears by God and does not break his oath, that whoever obeys the Messenger of God in his command and prohibition will never go astray nor be miserable. Guidance to every good lies within obedience to the Messenger of God ﷺ.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveying﴾, i.e., it is not upon the Messenger to guide hearts; rather, upon him is only the clear conveying and nothing else. So the Messenger does not bear the consequence of whoever disobeys, goes astray and perishes.

His saying, exalted be He, in verse [55]: ﴿God has promised those who believe among you﴾, i.e., who affirm God and His Messenger, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, so they establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. He promised them that He would make them successors in the earth, i.e., make them rulers and successors over its people, governing its inhabitants, a succession like that of those before them among the Children of Israel, when He drove out the Canaanites and the Amalekites from the land of Jerusalem and the Children of Israel inherited it. And His saying: ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, which is Islam, so He will make it prevail over all religion and preserve it from alteration, distortion and extinction until near the Hour. And His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And He will surely replace their fear with security﴾ — when this verse was revealed, the Muslims in Medina were in fear, none of them able to sleep with his sword far from him, because of the severity of fear from the disbelievers and hypocrites and the gathering of the confederates against them. God fulfilled for them what He had promised: He made them successors, established them, and replaced their fear with security. So to God belongs praise and grace.

His saying: ﴿They worship Me, not associating anything with Me﴾ — this is a praise of them and a reason for what He bestowed and gave them: they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. And they did so, and their remnants among the righteous still worship God alone to this day, not associating anything with Him. O God, make us among them. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that — it is those who are the defiantly disobedient﴾ is a warning and threat to whoever disbelieves after that great blessing and abundant bounty. Those are the defiant ones, who depart from God's command, leave His obedience, and deserve God's punishment and vengeance. We seek refuge in God; there is no power and no strength except with God.

Lessons of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The legitimacy of swearing by God Most High and the prohibition of swearing by other than Him.

2- Lack of trust in the hypocrites, for they lack what requires truthfulness in word and deed, which is faith.

3- Obedience to the Messenger of God brings guidance, for in it is the happiness of both abodes, and disobedience to him brings misguidance and loss.

4- The truth of God's promise to the people of faith and righteous deeds among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

5- The obligation to give thanks for blessings by worshipping God alone through the forms of worship He has legislated.

6- The severe warning to whoever is blessed by God with security, prosperity, sovereignty and honor, yet disbelieves these blessings and does not give thanks for them, thereby exposing them to extinction.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 53–55:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And they swore by God, their most solemn oaths﴾: i.e., they swore by God, exerting the utmost effort in their oaths.

﴿If you command them﴾: i.e., to go out to jihad.

﴿Obedience is known﴾: i.e., a known obedience to the Prophet in what he commands you and forbids you is better than your swearing by God.

﴿But if you turn away﴾: i.e., if you turn away, that is, you turn aside from obedience.

﴿Upon him is what he has been charged with﴾: i.e., the conveying of the message and its clarification by word and deed.

﴿And upon you is what you have been charged with﴾: i.e., the obligation to accept the Law and act upon it in belief, worship and judgment.

﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾: i.e., if you obey the Messenger in his command, his prohibition and his guidance, you will be guided to your own good.

﴿He will surely make them successors﴾: i.e., He will make them successors to others in the land, by replacing its former inhabitants for them, so that they will rule and govern it.

﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion﴾: i.e., by making Islam prevail over all other religions and preserving it from extinction.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of the state of the hypocrites. God informs about them with His words: ﴿And they swore by God, their most solemn oaths﴾, i.e., they swore to the Messenger ﷺ, exerting themselves to the utmost, saying: "If you command us to go out to jihad, we will surely go out with you." Here God commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Do not swear﴾, i.e., there is no need for oaths and their emphasis; rather, what is required is a known obedience from you to us, which will suffice you instead of oaths. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do﴾ is a rebuke and a discipline for them, as God informed them that He is aware of their secrets and of what they say and do in secret against the Messenger and the believers. Then God commanded His Messenger to say to them: Obey God and obey the Messenger in all that they command and forbid. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, i.e., you turn aside from obedience and reject it, then upon the Messenger is only what he has been charged with of conveying and clarifying, and upon you is what you have been charged with of the obligation to submit and obey. Whoever neglects his duty with which he has been entrusted will meet his recompense in full before his Lord.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided﴾ — this sentence is great in importance and noble in worth for the believer, who swears by God and does not break his oath, that whoever obeys the Messenger of God in his command and prohibition will never go astray nor be miserable. Guidance to every good lies within obedience to the Messenger of God ﷺ.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveying﴾, i.e., it is not upon the Messenger to guide hearts; rather, upon him is only the clear conveying and nothing else. So the Messenger does not bear the consequence of whoever disobeys, goes astray and perishes.

He promised them that He would make them successors in the earth, i.e., make them rulers and successors over its people, governing its inhabitants, a succession like that of those before them among the Children of Israel, when He drove out the Canaanites and the Amalekites from the land of Jerusalem and the Children of Israel inherited it. And His saying: ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, which is Islam, so He will make it prevail over all religion and preserve it from alteration, distortion and extinction until near the Hour. And they did so, and their remnants among the righteous still worship God alone to this day, not associating anything with Him. O God, make us among them. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that — it is those who are the defiantly disobedient﴾ is a warning and threat to whoever disbelieves after that great blessing and abundant bounty. Those are the defiant ones, who depart from God's command, leave His obedience, and deserve God's punishment and vengeance. We seek refuge in God; there is no power and no strength except with God.

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The legitimacy of swearing by God Most High and the prohibition of swearing by other than Him.

2- Lack of trust in the hypocrites, for they lack what requires truthfulness in word and deed, which is faith.

3- Obedience to the Messenger of God brings guidance, for in it is the happiness of both abodes, and disobedience to him brings misguidance and loss.

4- The truth of God's promise to the people of faith and righteous deeds among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

6- The severe warning to whoever is blessed by God with security, prosperity, sovereignty and honor, yet disbelieves these blessings and does not give thanks for them, thereby exposing them to extinction.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 56–57:

Explanation of the words:

"And establish the prayer" (wa-aqimu al-salah): That is, perform it in its complete and perfect form, observing its conditions (shurut), pillars (arkan), obligations (wajibat) and recommended acts (sunan), so that it bears fruit in the form of zakah (purification) and purity in your souls.

"And give zakah" (wa-atu al-zakah): That is, the obligatory zakah on silent wealth such as gold and silver and crops, and on livestock such as camels, cattle and sheep.

"And obey the Messenger" (wa-ati'u al-rasul): That is, Muhammad ﷺ, in his commands and prohibitions, and in accepting his guidance and direction.

"That you may receive mercy" (la'allakum turhamun): That is, in hope that your Lord will have mercy on you in your worldly life and in the Hereafter, so that He does not punish you in either of them.

"Escaping [Allah] in the earth" (mu'jizina fi al-ard): That is, escaping Allah the Exalted such that they cannot be overtaken and His vengeance and punishment do not descend upon them.

"And wretched is the destination" (wa-la-bi'sa al-masir): That is, the Fire, for it is the abode to which they retreat and to which they return.

The meaning of the two verses:

The Exalted commands His believing servants, from among the companions of the Noble Messenger, to establish the prayer, give zakah, and obey the Messenger ﷺ in his commands, prohibitions, guidance and direction, in hope that they will be shown mercy in both abodes and not be punished in either. Although this is initially addressed to the companions of the Messenger, it is general thereafter, encompassing every believing man and woman throughout life. His saying, ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve will escape [Allah] in the earth﴾, is an address to the Messenger ﷺ, in which his Lord forbids him from thinking that those who disbelieved, however great their power, will escape Allah the Exalted and flee from what He intends for them of disgrace and punishment. No! Rather, He will disgrace and humiliate them and give power over them, and He has done so. ﴿And their refuge is the Fire﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾: the Fire of Hell, to which they will return.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation of establishing the prayer, giving zakah and obeying the Messenger ﷺ, in order to obtain the mercy of Allah the Exalted in this world and the Hereafter: in this world through victory, empowerment, security and sovereignty, and in the Hereafter through entry into Paradise.

2- Affirmation of the helplessness of the disbelievers, and that they will never escape Allah the Exalted however great their power; His vengeance will descend upon them and His punishment will befall them.

3- Clarification of the fate of the people of disbelief, which is the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 58–60:

Explanation of the words:

*Liyasta'dhinkum* (let them seek permission from you): that is, let them ask your permission to enter upon you.

*Malakat aymanukum* (those whom your right hands possess): slaves, male and female.

*Lam yablughu al-hulm minkum* (have not reached puberty among you): that is, the age of legal responsibility, which is the time of wet dreams, fifteen years or more.

*Tada'una thiyabakum* (lay aside your garments): that is, at the time of the midday rest (qayluloh) for relaxation and sleep.

*Thalath 'awrat lakum* (three times of nakedness for you): 'awrah (nakedness, that which one feels shame in exposing) refers to these three times, when a person is uncovered in his bed, so they are three 'awrat.

*Ba'dahunna* (after them): that is, after the three mentioned times.

*Tawwafuna 'alaykum* (they go about you constantly): that is, for service.

*Ba'dukum 'ala ba'd* (some of you upon others): that is, some of you go about attending upon others.

*Fa-liyasta'dhinu* (then let them seek permission): that is, at all times, because they have become responsible adults.

*Wal-qawa'id min al-nisa'* (and women past child-bearing): that is, those who have ceased from menstruation and childbirth due to their advanced age.

*An yada'na thiyabahunna* (to lay aside their garments): such as the outer cloak (jilbab), the abaya, the face-veil (qina') and the head-covering (khimar).

*Ghayra mutabarrijatin bi-zinah* (without displaying adornment): that is, without displaying hidden adornment such as a necklace, bracelet and anklet.

*Wa-an yasta'fifna khayrun lahunna* (but to refrain is better for them): that is, not laying aside their garments is better for them than taking the concession.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. It is related concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse that the Prophet ﷺ sent a youth of the Ansar called Mudlij to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to summon him, and he found him asleep at midday. He knocked on the door and entered, and 'Umar awoke and something of him was uncovered. 'Umar then said: "I wish that Allah had forbidden our sons, our women and our servants from entering upon us at this hour except with permission." Then he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that this verse had been revealed, so he fell down in prostration in thanks to Allah, the Exalted.

So His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is an address to all believers in every age and land. And His saying ﴿Let those whom your right hands possess and those of you who have not reached puberty ask your permission﴾ means: teach your children and your servants to seek permission before entering upon you at these three times, and order them to do so. His saying ﴿three times﴾ is explained by His saying ﴿before the prayer of dawn﴾, which is the time of sleep at night; ﴿and when you lay aside your garments at midday﴾, which is the midday rest; and ﴿and after the prayer of 'isha'﴾, which is the beginning of night sleep. His saying ﴿three times of nakedness for you﴾ means these are the periods in which nakedness is exposed, so they were named 'awrah; and 'awrah is that which one feels shame in exposing. His saying ﴿there is no blame upon you or upon them﴾ means: nor upon the children and servants ﴿after these﴾, that is, after the three times. His saying ﴿they go about you﴾ means they enter and leave upon you for service. ﴿Some of you upon others﴾ means some of you enter upon others for service, and it is unavoidable, so there is no blame upon you at times other than these three.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ means: just as this clarification of the ruling on seeking permission has been made clear to you, Allah makes clear to you the verses containing the laws, rulings and manners; so to Him belongs praise and to Him belongs favour. His saying ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ means: of His creation and of what they need for their completion and happiness, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He prescribes for them and imposes upon them.

His saying, may He be exalted, in the second verse [59]: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾ means: when the child reaches the age of wet dreams, which is maturity, and has had a wet dream, then he must not enter upon anyone other than his mahram except after seeking permission, as men before him do. For by maturity, whose sign is wet dreams or reaching fifteen years or more, he has become a complete man, so he must not enter anyone's house except after seeking permission. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them seek permission as those before them sought permission﴾, namely the men. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾ means those containing His rulings and laws. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation and what is good for them, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His legislation, and this is a condition that obliges obedience to Him in what He commands and forbids. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And women past child-bearing who have no hope of marriage﴾ means those who have ceased from menstruation and childbirth due to their advanced age, such that they no longer hope for marriage and it is no longer hoped of them. For these there is no sin or blame in laying aside their khimar from above their heads, or their abaya over their garments that are on their bodies, provided they are not displaying adornment, that is, showing their adornment such as dyeing of the hands, bracelets on the wrists, anklets on the feet, or reddening of the lips, and whatever else is adornment that must be concealed. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But that they refrain is better for them﴾ means: whoever keeps to her khimar and abaya and does not display herself to strangers, uncovering her face and her attractions, is better in state and in outcome; and it is enough for her that Allah chooses for her, for what He chooses for her will only be good in this world and the Hereafter, so believing women should choose what Allah has chosen for them.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ means: He hears the words of His servants and knows their deeds and conditions, so let Him be feared and obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not disbelieved.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of teaching fathers, masters, children and servants to seek permission before entering upon them at the three mentioned times, which are expressed as 'awrat.

2- The obligation for children, once they have reached puberty, to seek permission before entering upon whomever they wish to enter in his house, because they have become responsible adults.

3- Clarification of the concession to uncover the face for a woman of an age in which she no longer menstruates or bears children, before non-mahram men; and if she maintains her covering and veiling, it would be better for her, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But that they refrain is better for them﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 58–60:

Explanation of the words:

*Liyasta'dhinkum* (let them seek permission from you): that is, let them ask your permission to enter upon you.

*Malakat aymanukum* (those whom your right hands possess): slaves, male and female.

*Lam yablughu al-hulm minkum* (have not reached puberty among you): that is, the age of legal responsibility, which is the time of wet dreams, fifteen years or more.

*Tada'una thiyabakum* (lay aside your garments): that is, at the time of the midday rest (qayluloh) for relaxation and sleep.

*Thalath 'awrat lakum* (three times of nakedness for you): 'awrah (nakedness, that which one feels shame in exposing) refers to these three times, when a person is uncovered in his bed, so they are three 'awrat.

*Ba'dahunna* (after them): that is, after the three mentioned times.

*Tawwafuna 'alaykum* (they go about you constantly): that is, for service.

*Ba'dukum 'ala ba'd* (some of you upon others): that is, some of you go about attending upon others.

*Fa-liyasta'dhinu* (then let them seek permission): that is, at all times, because they have become responsible adults.

*Wal-qawa'id min al-nisa'* (and women past child-bearing): that is, those who have ceased from menstruation and childbirth due to their advanced age.

*An yada'na thiyabahunna* (to lay aside their garments): such as the outer cloak (jilbab), the abaya, the face-veil (qina') and the head-covering (khimar).

*Ghayra mutabarrijatin bi-zinah* (without displaying adornment): that is, without displaying hidden adornment such as a necklace, bracelet and anklet.

*Wa-an yasta'fifna khayrun lahunna* (but to refrain is better for them): that is, not laying aside their garments is better for them than taking the concession.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. It is related concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse that the Prophet ﷺ sent a youth of the Ansar called Mudlij to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to summon him, and he found him asleep at midday. He knocked on the door and entered, and 'Umar awoke and something of him was uncovered. 'Umar then said: "I wish that Allah had forbidden our sons, our women and our servants from entering upon us at this hour except with permission." Then he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that this verse had been revealed, so he fell down in prostration in thanks to Allah, the Exalted.

So His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O you who have believed﴾ is an address to all believers in every age and land. And His saying ﴿Let those whom your right hands possess and those of you who have not reached puberty ask your permission﴾ means: teach your children and your servants to seek permission before entering upon you at these three times, and order them to do so. His saying ﴿three times﴾ is explained by His saying ﴿before the prayer of dawn﴾, which is the time of sleep at night; ﴿and when you lay aside your garments at midday﴾, which is the midday rest; and ﴿and after the prayer of 'isha'﴾, which is the beginning of night sleep. His saying ﴿three times of nakedness for you﴾ means these are the periods in which nakedness is exposed, so they were named 'awrah; and 'awrah is that which one feels shame in exposing. His saying ﴿there is no blame upon you or upon them﴾ means: nor upon the children and servants ﴿after these﴾, that is, after the three times. His saying ﴿they go about you﴾ means they enter and leave upon you for service. ﴿Some of you upon others﴾ means some of you enter upon others for service, and it is unavoidable, so there is no blame upon you at times other than these three.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ means: just as this clarification of the ruling on seeking permission has been made clear to you, Allah makes clear to you the verses containing the laws, rulings and manners; so to Him belongs praise and to Him belongs favour. His saying ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ means: of His creation and of what they need for their completion and happiness, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He prescribes for them and imposes upon them.

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them seek permission as those before them sought permission﴾, namely the men. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾ means those containing His rulings and laws. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation and what is good for them, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His legislation, and this is a condition that obliges obedience to Him in what He commands and forbids. For these there is no sin or blame in laying aside their khimar from above their heads, or their abaya over their garments that are on their bodies, provided they are not displaying adornment, that is, showing their adornment such as dyeing of the hands, bracelets on the wrists, anklets on the feet, or reddening of the lips, and whatever else is adornment that must be concealed. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But that they refrain is better for them﴾ means: whoever keeps to her khimar and abaya and does not display herself to strangers, uncovering her face and her attractions, is better in state and in outcome; and it is enough for her that Allah chooses for her, for what He chooses for her will only be good in this world and the Hereafter, so believing women should choose what Allah has chosen for them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verse 61:

Explanation of the words:

Al-haraj (حرج): constriction; here it means sin, i.e., there is no sin upon those mentioned in eating with others.

Aw ma malaktum mafatihahu (أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه): that which is under your control, either by ownership or by agency, such as being an agent over an orchard or livestock.

Aw sadiqikum (أو صديقكم): i.e., one whose friendship you have affirmed and who has affirmed his friendship to you.

Jami'an aw ashtatan (جميعاً أو أشتاتاً): i.e., gathered together at the meal or scattered.

Min 'indi Allah (من عند الله): because He is the One who legislated it and commanded it, and whatever is from Allah is a great good.

Tayyibah (طيبة): i.e., the soul of the Muslim who is greeted is made content by it.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the guidance of the believers and the explanation of what perfects and makes them happy. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, lifted from them a great constriction that they had felt and that pained them. They had seen that eating with those who have infirmities, namely the blind, the lame, the sick, and the chronically afflicted, might result in their eating what is not lawful for them, since people with these infirmities do not eat as healthy people do, in quantity or in manner, and Allah says: ﴿And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 188]. Likewise, the people with infirmities felt constricted about eating with the healthy, fearing that they might be disgusted by them, and this pained them. So Allah revealed this verse, lifting the constriction from everyone, both the healthy and the people with infirmities, and He said: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or from that whose keys you hold﴾ by agency or otherwise, ﴿or from your friend﴾, meaning one whose friendship you have affirmed and who has affirmed his friendship to you, so long as consent is present, whether or not they are present and without seeking permission, and even if they are present.

Allah also lifted from them another constriction: some of them felt constricted about eating alone and would see that they should eat only with others. Some also felt constricted about eating communally, fearing that they might harm the one eating with them. Allah lifted all of that by His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together﴾, i.e., gathered around one portion, ﴿or separately﴾, i.e., scattered, each eating alone whenever he wishes. All of this arises from their piety toward Allah and their fear of His disobedience, since He had forbidden them to consume one another's wealth unjustly in His saying: ﴿And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 188].

As for His saying: ﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good﴾, He guided them to what brings about affection, purity of hearts, and joy among them: that whoever enters a house, whether his own or another's, should greet the people of the house, saying, "Peace be upon you." If the house has no one in it, or is a mosque, he says, "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah." His saying ﴿a greeting from Allah﴾ means that it is He who commanded it and guided to it. His saying ﴿blessed﴾ means full of blessing that returns to everyone. That it is ﴿good﴾ means that the souls of those greeted are made content by it.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you, that you may understand﴾, i.e., just as He has made clear to you the rulings and etiquettes, Allah makes clear to you the verses bearing the laws and rulings, in hope that you will understand from Allah His legislation and His rulings, and act upon them, so that you become perfected and happy through them.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The general permission to eat with those who have infirmities, without constriction from either party.

2- Permission to eat from the houses of those mentioned in the verse among relatives and friends.

3- The permissibility of eating communally and individually without constriction.

4- The legitimacy of greeting upon entering houses, and that in it there is good and merit.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 24, verses 62–64:

Explanation of the words:

Amr jami' (a gathering matter): such as the Friday sermon and the like, or any matter whose attendance is obligatory, such as a gathering for an important affair like war or the like.

Yasta'dhinuhu (they ask his permission): that is, they ask the Prophet ﷺ for permission.

Li-ba'di sha'nihim (for some of their affairs): that is, for some of their own private matters.

Du'a' al-Rasul (the calling of the Messenger): that is, his calling. So one does not say "O Muhammad," but says "O Prophet of Allah" or "O Messenger of Allah."

Ka-du'a' ba'dikum ba'dan (like the calling of some of you to one another): that is, as some of you call one another, for example "O 'Umar" or "O Sa'id."

Yatasallalna minkum liwadhan (slipping away from among you, concealing themselves): that is, they slip away one by one, each one covering the other, until they leave secretly.

An tusibahum fitnah (lest a trial befall them): that is, a deviation in their hearts, so that they become disbelievers.

Qad ya'lamu ma antum 'alayh (He certainly knows what you are upon): that is, of faith and hypocrisy, and of the intention for good or the intention for evil. The word "qad" here is for emphasis, and it is treated as it would be in the sense of "rubba" (perhaps), since it is for lessening, though it sometimes serves to indicate abundance.

Meaning of the verses:

He, the Exalted, informs that the complete believers in their faith are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and that when they are with him ﷺ in a matter of gathering that requires their presence, such as the Friday prayer and gatherings for war, they do not leave until they ask his permission ﷺ and he grants it to them. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Only those are believers who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern, they do not depart until they have asked his permission.﴾

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will among them and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ In this is instruction for the Messenger and the believers, and an allusion to the hypocrites. He, the Exalted, has informed that those who ask the Prophet's permission are the believers in Allah and His Messenger, and by contrast, those who do not ask permission and leave without leave are those who do not believe in Allah and His Messenger, and they are the hypocrites in truth. He commanded the Messenger of Allah, when the believers ask his permission for some of their affairs, to grant permission to whomever he wills of those whose presence is not important, just as He commanded him to ask Allah's forgiveness for them, for what may be an excuse not legally permitting them to seek leave, and for their hope of forgiveness by His saying: "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like the calling of some of you to others.﴾ This admits of several meanings, all of them true. The first: that the believers should be careful not to anger the Messenger of Allah by opposing him, for if he calls upon them they will be destroyed, since the supplication of the Messenger is not rejected; he is not like the supplication of others. The second: that they should not call the Messenger by his name, "O Muhammad" or "O Ahmad," but must say "O Prophet of Allah" or "O Messenger of Allah." The third: that they should not be harsh in expression, but should soften their speech and gentle their wording, out of reverence and veneration for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is what His saying, the Exalted, comprises: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like the calling of some of you to others.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, informed them that He certainly knows those hypocrites who are present in a gathering with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and slip away one after another without asking permission, hiding behind one another in their flight from the assembly, each covering the other. In this is a very grave warning to those hypocrites.

And His saying: ﴿So let those who oppose his order beware lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment reach them.﴾ That is, the order of the Messenger of Allah. This is general for the believers and the hypocrites and until the Day of Resurrection. So let them beware lest a trial befall them, which is a deviation in their hearts, so that they die as disbelievers, or a painful punishment strike them in this world, and punishments are of many kinds and forms.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, by creation, dominion and ownership, and they are servants who dispose of themselves as He wills and decree what He desires. Unquestionably, let them fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning His Messenger, so that they do not oppose his command or disobey his prohibition, for Allah has sent no messenger except to be obeyed by His permission.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He already knows what you are upon.﴾ This is a statement that carries threat and warning as well. What people hold of outward and inward sayings is known to Allah, the Exalted, and on the Day they return to Allah after their death, He will inform them of what they did of good and evil and will recompense them with the fullest recompense. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ So let them beware of opposing His Messenger or disobeying him, and let them fear Him concerning His command and prohibition, for His retribution is severe and His punishment is harsh.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of seeking permission from the leader of the Muslims when the matter is one of common concern, and the leader may grant permission to whom he wills and leave aside whom he wills according to the public interest.

2- The obligation of venerating the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the prohibition of disrespect toward him, while living and after death.

3- The obligation of obeying the Messenger of Allah and the prohibition of opposing his command and prohibition.

4- Whoever is bold enough to treat the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ lightly is feared to die with a bad ending, and we seek refuge in Allah.

This is what His saying, the Exalted, comprises: ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like the calling of some of you to others.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, informed them that He certainly knows those hypocrites who are present in a gathering with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and slip away one after another without asking permission, hiding behind one another in their flight from the assembly, each covering the other. In this is a very grave warning to those hypocrites.

And His saying: ﴿So let those who oppose his order beware lest a trial strike them or a painful punishment reach them.﴾ That is, the order of the Messenger of Allah. This is general for the believers and the hypocrites and until the Day of Resurrection. So let them beware lest a trial befall them, which is a deviation in their hearts, so that they die as disbelievers, or a painful punishment strike them in this world, and punishments are of many kinds and forms.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, by creation, dominion and ownership, and they are servants who dispose of themselves as He wills and decree what He desires. Unquestionably, let them fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning His Messenger, so that they do not oppose his command or disobey his prohibition, for Allah has sent no messenger except to be obeyed by His permission.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He already knows what you are upon.﴾ This is a statement that carries threat and warning as well. What people hold of outward and inward sayings is known to Allah, the Exalted, and on the Day they return to Allah after their death, He will inform them of what they did of good and evil and will recompense them with the fullest recompense. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ So let them beware of opposing His Messenger or disobeying him, and let them fear Him concerning His command and prohibition, for His retribution is severe and His punishment is harsh.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of seeking permission from the leader of the Muslims when the matter is one of common concern, and the leader may grant permission to whom he wills and leave aside whom he wills according to the public interest.

2- The obligation of venerating the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the prohibition of disrespect toward him, while living and after death.

3- The obligation of obeying the Messenger of Allah and the prohibition of opposing his command and prohibition.

4- Whoever is bold enough to treat the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ lightly is feared to die with a bad ending, and we seek refuge in Allah.
